papers.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
papers.abstract: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions. With this data, we find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore that the reality of the higher Gauss sums suffices for time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories, and propose a refined criterion. We demonstrate the scalability of this gated implementation by identifying prime modular data at rank 100 that is not realized by any Chern-Simons theory. The identified data through rank 42 has been made available at https://AnyonAtlas.org, to which further data will be added as it is found.

papers.title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and Mordell-Weil lattices
papers.abstract: Let $X\to B$ be a Weierstrass fibration with integral fibers from a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold to a del Pezzo surface. For a smooth curve $D\subset B$ with smooth inverse image $Y$, we decompose the moduli fiber of stable sheaves with Euler characteristic one and projected cycle $D$. In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing. For infinitesimally rigid sections we compute the GV contributions, recovering the $E_8$ theta product over a $(-1)$-curve. We formulate the corresponding conjecture for families of sections.

papers.title: Grade Restriction Rule For D-Brane Transport In Non-Abelian Gauged Linear Sigma Models
papers.abstract: We study the low energy behaviour of B-type D-branes in non-Abelian gauged linear sigma models. The main problem is to determine the grade restriction rule for D-brane transport from one phase to another along paths. We analyze the convergence condition of the integral for the hemisphere partition function. We perform a thorough analysis in a particular model with two phases, one weakly coupled and one strongly coupled, both corresponding to Calabi-Yau threefolds. General methods are developed in this study and are applied to other models successfully. The integrals for a set of special Chan-Paton representations exhibit critical behaviour around each singular point on the phase boundary. From each of these points emanate ``no entry zones'' where a convergent contour is lost or is forced to traverse Gamma function poles. Knowledge of the special representations and no entry zones is strong enough to uniquely determine the grade restriction rule. In the course of this study, we encounter a problem in Weyl invariance of convergent contours, which forces us to modify the grade restriction criterion. The special representations play an important r\^ole in the monodromy around the singular point. We also obtain exact results on boundary conditions in supersymmetric QCDs and apply them to understand the low energy behaviour of D-branes in the strong coupling phase.

papers.title: Holomorphic Floer theory I: exponential integrals in finite and infinite dimensions
papers.abstract: In the first of the series of papers devoted to our project ``Holomorphic Floer Theory" we discuss exponential integrals and related wall-crossing structures. We emphasize two points of view on the subject: the one based on the ideas of deformation quantization and the one based on the ideas of Floer theory. Their equivalence is a corollary of our generalized Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. In the case of exponential integrals this amounts to several comparison isomorphisms between local and global versions of de Rham and Betti cohomology. We develop the corresponding theories in particular generalizing Morse-Novikov theory to the holomorphic case. We prove that arising wall-crossing structures are analytic. As a corollary, perturbative expansions of exponential integrals are resurgent. Based on a careful study of finite-dimensional exponential integrals we propose a conjectural approach to infinite-dimensional exponential integrals. We illustrate this approach in the case of Feynman path integral with holomorphic Lagrangian boundary conditions as well as in the case of the complexified Chern-Simons theory. We discuss the arising perverse sheaf of infinite rank as well as analyticity of the corresponding ``Chern-Simons wall-crossing structure". We develop a general theory of quantum wave functions and show that in the case of Chern-Simons theory it gives an alternative description of the Chern-Simons wall-crossing structure based on the notion of generalized Nahm sum. We propose several conjectures about analyticity and resurgence of the corresponding perturbative series.

papers.title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
papers.abstract: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(\tau_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence. We include a User's Guide to the HASS and several worked examples, as well as hastened Adams charts for many commonly encountered $\mathcal{A}(1)$-modules.

papers.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
papers.abstract: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In the Kirkwood-Dirac phase-space formalism, the spatiotemporal distribution and the cost function are complex-valued, and the spatiotemporal couplings are Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions that yield the correct marginals for the local states. In the spatiotemporal state formalism, the cost operators are generally non-Hermitian, and the spatiotemporal couplings are generally non-Hermitian and yield the correct reduced local states. The Margenau-Hill phase-space distribution gives rise to a real-valued optimal transport in spatiotemporal phase space; in the spatiotemporal state formalism, this corresponds to a Hermitian spatiotemporal coupling state. We give a rigorous definitions and a careful discussion of its duality. We also introduce a spatiotemporal quantum Wasserstein metric based on a metric in spatiotemporal phase spaces and show that it satisfies the metric axioms.

papers.title: General Lagrangian formulations for mixed-antisymmetric tensor fields on flat backgrounds
papers.abstract: We present, for the first time, local Lagrangian formulations for (ir)reducible integer higher-spin massless and massive Poincare group representations subject to Young tableau with $k$ columns $Y[\hat{s}_1,\hat{s}_2,...,\hat{s}_k]$ in $d$-dimensional Minkowski space-time. The particles are described in a metric-like formulation by tensor fields carrying $k$ groups of antisymmetric Lorentz indices $\Phi_{\mu^1[{\hat{s}_1}],\mu^2[{\hat{s}_2}],..., \mu^k[{\hat{s}_k}]}$ using the BRST procedure with both the complete operator $Q$ and incomplete $Q_c$ BRST operators. Starting from a description of bosonic mixed-antisymmetric higher-spin fields in terms of an auxiliary Fock space associated with a special Poincare module, we realize a conversion of the initial operator constraint system into a system of first-class operator constraints. For this purpose, we find, for the first time, by means of Verma module the auxiliary representations of the constraint subalgebra, to be isomorphic due to Howe duality to $so(k,k)$ algebra, and containing the subsystem of second-class operators in terms of new oscillator variables forming the Fock module. An unconstrained (with $Q$) and constrained (with $Q_c$ and BRST invariant algebraic constraints) gauge Lagrangian formulations with equivalent dynamics, but different configuration spaces are found. We outline within $Q_c$-approach the concept of consistent local cubic interactions and evaluate the candidate structure of cubic vertices involving $p\geq 3$ copies of interacting massless mixed-antisymmetric fields.

papers.title: Charged Schr\"odinger blocks in $1+1$ dimensions from the quartic Casimir and endpoint equations
papers.abstract: We construct charge-two Schr\"odinger conformal blocks in one spatial dimension, independently of any dynamical realization. We consider ordered vacuum four-point functions of fundamental fields of dimension $1/2$, with homogeneous Schr\"odinger equations at the earliest and latest insertions and interactions allowed in the intermediate two-particle interval. For reduced blocks analytic in signed spatial coordinates and even under simultaneous spatial inversion, two functions of the time cross-ratio determine the full spatial dependence: the collinear value and a rescaled mixed spatial derivative. An exact Kummer lift, built from confluent hypergeometric functions, gives this reconstruction. An operator identity reduces the quartic Casimir equation, modulo the endpoint equations, to an equivalent coupled system for this pair. At generic exchanged dimension, OPE conditions select a unique block up to normalization for each primary parity. We obtain collinear ${}_4F_3$ functions and sums of Kummer products, including the shadow branches. The blocks depend on the relative sign of the signed coordinates, distinguishing piecewise linear worldlines with an inflection from those with monotone segment velocities. In the Calogero model, we recover the previously derived bosonic four-point function and obtain its fermionic counterpart, with an independent integral check. At the diffusion-limited fixed point of $A+B\to\emptyset$, two blocks of opposite primary parity give the same collinear unlike-species response. Nonnegativity for all positions and ordered times selects the even family, thereby establishing that the response summed over species contains the even shadow pair with dimensions $\Delta=1,2$. The nonnegativity argument demonstrates a concrete constraint for a Schr\"odinger bootstrap beyond collinear data.

papers.title: Spectrum of the parity operator for parafermions and parabosons from character formulas
papers.abstract: In a recent paper [J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 59 175201 (2026)] Green's triple relations for parafermions and parabosons were extended by including a new operator $P$, referred to as the parity operator. The spectrum of $P$ in Fock space representations was computed, making use of the action of parafermion (resp.\ paraboson) creation and annihilation operators. In the current paper, we adopt a different method to compute the spectrum of $P$, namely using character formulas. For a set of $n$ parafermions, the action of $P$ is deduced from character formulas of $so(2n+2)$. For a set of $n$ parabosons, the known spectrum of $P$ yields new character formulas of particular $osp(2|2n)$ representations.

papers.title: Whitehead doubles and the failure of the AJ conjecture
papers.abstract: For marked Whitehead doubles of torus knots with coprime parameters $2\le r<s$, the AJ conjecture fails for both clasp signs, both companion chiralities, and every integer twist. The zero-framed signed unreduced colored Jones sequence has a nonzero rationally saturated annihilator. Every nonzero primitive representative specializes nontrivially at $t=-1$ with the meridian variable $M$ independent. With $L$ the longitude variable, the specialization contains the irreducible quadratic $E=L^2-(M^4-4M^2+1)L+M^4$ for the negative clasp and $M^4E(M^{-1},L)$ for the positive clasp. The corresponding quadratic is coprime to the full classical $A$-polynomial, including $L-1$, over $\mathbb{Q}(M)[L^{\pm1}]$, so the discrepancy persists when each irreducible factor is counted once. The curve $E=0$ comes from the marked Whitehead link exterior with its axis cusp complete. For the displayed monic polynomial, $\pi m(E)$ is the unsigned volume of that two-cusped exterior. We use the actual Jones sequence to select a right divisor of the satellite transfer operator. Rational factor tests show that the quadratic survives in this divisor, and the two marked companion fillings exclude it as a component of the satellite boundary curve.

papers.title: Commuting integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs revisited: certified densities, spectral rigidity, and an exact identification at the c=1 branch point
papers.abstract: We revisit the commuting local integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs constructed in hep-th/0404195 as input data for integrable boundary states, using exact-arithmetic operator-product engines. A bootstrap lemma reduces its overdetermined bilinear commutativity systems to a distinguished odd charge D plus linear kernel problems -- conditionally on even-spin vacancy, a machine-verified but finite-range input. For the Z_2 x Z_2 "paperclip" family we publish the spin-7 density P_8, prove [I_3,I_5]=[I_3,I_7]=[I_5,I_7]=0 identically in n, and verify the Lukyanov-Vitchev-Zamolodchikov four-screening characterization at spins 7 and 9 at sampled n. For the A_2^(2) family we give an exact Coulomb-gas dictionary to the dual Phi_{1,2}/Phi_{2,1} perturbations (that identification itself being classical, Zamolodchikov; Smirnov), whence the infinite hierarchy at all spins 6n+-1 follows by the Feigin-Frenkel affine-Toda theorem; our contribution is the certified dictionary, not a new all-spin construction. At c=1 the tower's defining charges are exactly quantum KdV at c_{1,4}=-25/2 -- the all-odd sector of the Freeman-Hornfeck-West family: the hierarchy embeds at every odd spin, equality verified through spin 15, all-spin multiplicity one open. We exclude or disfavor the named non-KdV candidates at the tested loci and identify the self-dual degeneracy as L(1,0). Through spin 11, the generic centralizer of I_3 is, for all three Z_2 x O(N) "cylindrical" families, one-dimensional at odd and zero at even spins, with Q(t)-symbolic charges at spins 7, 9, 11 and an explained fiber jump at N=-2. We certify the published 2004 low-spin formulas and record five corrections (one presumed). All-spin statements are made only where proved, finite-range otherwise. We close with a corank-character conjecture linking the rank deficiencies of the bilinear systems to characters of screening kernels.

papers.title: Exact Solutions to Matrix Models and String Theories: The Global Construction
papers.abstract: Exact nonperturbative solutions to matrix models and string theories are obtained in closed-form via a discrete-Fourier/Zak-transform representation of their partition-function resurgent-transseries. Examples include all hermitian one-matrix models (paired with their topological string duals) alongside all their multicritical and minimal-string double-scaling limits. The resulting structure is resonant, necessarily including both eigenvalues (D-branes) and anti-eigenvalues (negative-tension-branes). In a complementary preceding paper these solutions were extensively verified at the local level. In order to study them globally across their phase diagrams, complete non-linear Stokes data (and corresponding connection formulae) are still needed -- all of which are obtained herein. This involves a careful study of (anti-) eigenvalue tunneling across the complete multi-sheeted structure of their associated spectral-curves, and how the result descends from multi-cut smooth-curves to single-cut singular-curves -- all of which are extensively checked via large-order analysis and matrix-integral computations. Making use of the resulting exact Stokes automorphisms, nonperturbative solutions can be fully tested, from weak-to-strong 't Hooft coupling, as well as from large-to-small N, and for any complex-values of all parameters, by correctly implementing Stokes-transitions at the crossing of all possible Stokes-lines. Several analytical and numerical tests are carried through in diverse examples covering from matrix models through non-critical strings, which produce very sharp numerical matches fully validating our exact analytical expressions. Anti-eigenvalues or negative-tension D-branes are an absolutely essential part of the story in order to find such precise agreements.

papers.title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
papers.abstract: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

papers.title: Charge at regular centers in curvature-coupled electrodynamics
papers.abstract: An electric or magnetic flux through shrinking symmetry spheres ordinarily produces an $r^{-4}$ Maxwell stress and a singular center. We examine how this obstruction changes when the Maxwell invariant is multiplied by an arbitrary scalar-curvature response $h(R)$. For real, static, spherically symmetric solutions, the difference between the radial and temporal gravitational equations gives a linear equation for a composite response variable. Combined with the trace equation, it bounds the response-weighted Maxwell source whenever the Kretschmann scalar is bounded, without assuming a limit or derivative bounds for the Ricci scalar. Magnetic and electric displacement charges cannot coexist, and neither charge is possible if $h$ remains bounded and bounded away from zero. On either surviving charged branch, the Ricci scalar converges and the weighted source tends to zero. Magnetic charge requires $h=o(r^4)$, whereas electric displacement requires $r^4|h|\to\infty$. Exact solutions show that these thresholds are sharp and realize the $r^6$ magnetic and $r^{-6}$ electric rates for a smooth geometric center. We also classify the zero-response sector, where an electric field may survive even though its displacement charge vanishes.

papers.title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
papers.abstract: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

papers.title: Information geometry and entanglement under phase-space deformation through nonsymplectic congruence transformation
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between Fisher-Rao (FR) information geometry and Gaussian quantum correlations under nonsymplectic phase-space transformations, with particular emphasis on noncommutative (NC) deformation implemented through the Bopp shift. Using the established affine invariance of the FR-metric, we examine the transformation properties of Gaussian covariance matrices and the positive partial transpose (PPT) criterion under invertible congruence transformations. For a bipartite Gaussian system, we demonstrate that keeping the canonical partial-transpose (PT) matrix fixed in the deformed phase space produces deformation-dependent spectral shifts that may cross the conventional PPT threshold. When the PT operation is transported together with the covariance and commutation matrices, the physical PPT spectrum and separability classification remain invariant under local Darboux transformations. We further investigate a two-dimensional anisotropic oscillator in NC phase space, where the deformation parameters modify the effective canonical Hamiltonian and consequently influence the Gaussian ground-state correlations and entanglement between canonical modes. The corresponding FR-geometry reveals that the original covariance manifold possesses constant negative scalar curvature. In contrast, the pure symmetric normal-form covariance family is intrinsically one-dimensional and flat. These results distinguish the statistical geometry of Gaussian covariance matrices from the physical quantum correlations determined by the Hamiltonian, commutation structure, and subsystem decomposition.

papers.title: Computing $F$-Symbols from Modular Data
papers.abstract: We present a strategy for computing the $F$-symbols of unitary modular categories with a self-dual simple generator, starting from their modular data, which almost entirely avoids the non-linear solution of the pentagon equations. The algorithm climbs a ladder of braid group representations on successively more strands of the generator until enough $F$-symbols have been determined to propagate them to a complete solution. The strategy presented is successful in difficult cases through ranks 11 and 12, including $\operatorname{Z}(\mathrm{Haagerup}_3)$, and does not require the category to be multiplicity-free. Although the algorithm is implemented numerically, we describe a reliable means of recovering the exact $F$-symbols, assuming that in some gauge they lie in a given number field, and of certifying every pentagon and hexagon equation exactly. The exotic rank-11 anisotropic modular category B11-00119 (https://anyonatlas.org/data/B11-00119), with largest fusion coefficient 4, is used as a motivating example, for which the solve takes roughly 10 minutes on a laptop. We will continue to add $F$-symbol solutions to https://AnyonAtlas.org as they are completed.

papers.title: Quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with nontrivial sound speed in inflation
papers.abstract: In this work, we systematically investigate the quantum-information diagnostics of cosmological perturbations with a nontrivial sound speed, utilizing a normalized open two-mode squeezed-state framework. Rather than introducing new observables, our analysis focuses on how a modified sound speed dynamically reshapes the Schr\"odinger evolution of the squeezing parameters ($r_k$ and $\phi_k$). We demonstrate how these dynamical changes are inherited by the reduced density matrix of the observable sector. By employing a sound-speed-resonance parametrization, we derive and evaluate the purity, von Neumann entropy, R\'enyi entropies, and logarithmic negativity. We introduce a bounded variable $x = \tanh r_k$ and perform numerical simulations within the inflationary regime. Our numerical results reveal that a nontrivial sound speed significantly suppresses the purity of the reduced state, indicating enhanced effective mixedness. Simultaneously, it strongly amplifies and modulates both the entropic and entanglement diagnostics. More precisely, a nontrivial sound speed postpones the onset of classicality by modulating the decoherence process. Ultimately, we show that a nontrivial sound speed leaves distinct and identifiable quantum-information signatures within the entanglement structure of the early universe.

papers.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a magnetic spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal has a maximum at $2k_c$ and, as expected from momentum conservation, has a sharp cutoff at that scale. We apply this analysis to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160$ MeV the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-10 MeV on such viable models.

papers.title: Dynamics of a spinning body with scalar multipoles
papers.abstract: We construct an effective worldline action for a spinning compact object in theories of gravity with massless, non-minimally coupled scalar fields. To this end, we generalize the standard skeletonized approach used in General Relativity to model the stress-energy tensor of a small body in a background spacetime, dressing its multipolar structure with the scalar field. Within a pole-dipole approximation, we derive a modified set of Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations of motion for the spinning body, together with the field equations for the scalar field and the metric. We consider both parity-even and parity-odd scalars. We tailor this formalism to model the evolution of asymmetric binaries, such as Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs), by systematically expanding the relevant equations in powers of the binary mass ratio and deriving the dynamics up to first post-adiabatic (1PA) order, along with the self-force equations needed to determine the particle's acceleration. For a parity-even scalar, the 1PA dynamics depends only on the mass, spin, and scalar charge of the secondary, plus a single self-coupling constant. For a pseudoscalar, we find that the binary dynamics coincides with General Relativity through 1PA.

papers.title: An energy-dependent rescaling of the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian: Standard Model Extension identification, matter sector, and long-baseline degeneracy
papers.abstract: We study the consequences of multiplying the neutrino propagation Hamiltonian by a real, energy-dependent scalar, $H_\eta(E)=f(E)H_0(E)$ with $f(E)=1-\eta_0(E/E_0)^2$, a minimal-length ansatz. Its vacuum part is a dimension-four, CPT-even Lorentz-violating term of the Standard Model Extension with coefficient $(\cL)_{ii}=-\eta_0(m_i^2-m_1^2)/(2E_0^2)$, diagonal in the mass basis and fixed by the mass matrix, hence removable by a reparametrization. The matter-potential rescaling has dimension-five behaviour and is CPT-odd. For $f=1-\eta_0(E/E_0)^p$ the vacuum term behaves as a dimension $p+2$ operator and the matter term as $p+3$, so only $p=2$ gives a marginal vacuum operator; $p=0$ is absorbed into the measured mass splittings, and non-integer $p$ admits no local operator. For $\eta_0=0.02$ at $E_0=2.5$~GeV we find $|(\cL)_{33}|\simeq4\times10^{-24}$, comparable to present atmospheric bounds, whereas a Planck-suppressed deformation with $\beta_0=\mathcal{O}(1)$ gives $3.2\times10^{-58}$. At constant density it is equivalent to $L\to f(E)L$: mixing angles and the Dirac phase are unchanged, the CP asymmetry is reparametrized rather than generated, and the leading observable is a rescaling of $\dm_{31}$. At $1297$~km a re-fit of $\dm_{31}$ alone absorbs $23$~per cent of the squared probability difference, and a four-parameter re-fit absorbs $41.5$~per cent. No statistical analysis is performed; degeneracy means a distance in probability space, not a confidence interval.

papers.title: Localizing the M-Theory Path Integral: Membrane Instantons
papers.abstract: We propose a formula for M2-instanton contributions to the M-theory path integral, incorporating quantum corrections to all orders in the Planck length. The M2-brane action is determined by relative equivariant localization, while an equivariant Dolbeault character computes the one-loop determinant. Continuous families of M2-branes are treated by equivariant localization on their moduli spaces. For M-theory backgrounds dual to ABJM theory, we compute single instanton contributions from linear holomorphic fillings to the sphere partition function and the topologically twisted index associated with supersymmetric $AdS_4$ black holes. Our results reproduce known field theory instanton coefficients and give new analytic predictions for mass and squashing deformations at all Chern-Simons levels. For the $V^{5,2}$ theory, we compute new instanton contributions and establish an exact relation between its partition function at special squashing and that of ABJM theory on the round three-sphere.

papers.title: A Positive Metric on Four-Dimensional QFTs
papers.abstract: A natural metric on the space of four-dimensional quantum field theories was introduced by Jack and Osborn in classic work on the local renormalization group. In perturbation theory, the Jack-Osborn metric determines the flow of the $a$-anomaly, and positivity implies the $a$-theorem. We derive a non-perturbative generalization of the Jack-Osborn metric and show that it is non-negative by the averaged null energy condition (ANEC). Consequently, the ANEC implies the strong $a$-theorem, and provides the monotonic function along the flow. The method is based on spectral analysis of the three-point function $\langle \mathcal{O}_I \mathcal{E} \mathcal{O}_J\rangle$, where the $\mathcal{O}_I$ are relevant operators and $\mathcal{E}$ is the averaged null energy. This three-point function is decomposed under the spectrum of null rotations that fix the light ray, leading to a positivity condition at each impact parameter.

papers.title: Horizon kinematics and the fine structure induced by finite-energy Hawking radiation
papers.abstract: Hawking radiation can modify the horizon structure of a black hole through the loss of mass and global charges. Investigating this process through quantum tunneling, we develop a systematic strategy to reconstruct horizon displacements under finite-energy emission, even when their radii are not explicitly known. Inversion of the horizon condition allows to follow roots's displacements along sequences of static geometries. As a concrete realization, we consider a nonlinearly charged extension of the Ba\~nados--Teitelboim--Zanelli (BTZ) family, whose horizon structure offers an ideal setup to explore this process. Of particular interest is an initial configuration with a double inner horizon coexisting with a simple event horizon. We show that neutral emission necessarily splits the inner root into two simple ones, revealing a horizon fine structure. For charged emission, the dependence of extracted charge on emitted energy determines the separation law and allows that preservation or later restore the degeneracy. We construct such channels connecting the same initial and final states through distinct internal histories sharing the same leading semiclassical factor. As emission continues, the larger of the newly separated inner horizons can coalesce with the event horizon, driving the sequence towards extremality with a vanishing temperature but finite tunneling probability. We find that zero temperature cannot be attained in finite boundary time while uniform adiabaticity bounds hold. We also establish a regime where the geometric expansion and the canonical thermal approximation remain controlled near this endpoint. Finally, applying this analysis to the sector reproducing a quantum-backreacted BTZ geometry reveals how the leading semiclassical corrections raise the temperature and enhance the neutral-probe horizon emission factor relative to classical BTZ.

papers.title: Melvin-type Electromagnetized Kerr Black Hole in Kaluza-Klein and Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion Theories
papers.abstract: A naive application of solution-generating techniques to construct Melvin-type rotating black holes in the Kaluza-Klein (KK) theory in the presence of both electric and magnetic external fields generically introduces an undesirable Taub-swirling twist term. We investigate its origin and modify the electromagnetization procedure, thereby constructing an exact solution of the Melvin-type electromagnetized Kerr black hole in the KK theory without the swirling term. We also obtain the analogous solution in the Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton-axion (EMDA) theory. The modified solution-generating techniques allow one to introduce both the dyonic charges and external electromagnetic fields independently into Ricci-flat seed metrics in both theories, without generating either Taub-NUT or Taub-swirling twists.

papers.title: Non-Perturbative Moduli Stabilization with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ Modular Symmetry
papers.abstract: We study the stabilization of the three complex moduli associated with Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ modular symmetry by gaugino condensation in $\mathcal N=1$ supergravity models from heterotic string theory, where one-loop threshold corrections fix both the modular weight and the singularity structure of the superpotential. We determine, for each threshold class, the complete parametrization of the consistent superpotential relying on Sp$(4,\mathbb Z)$ basic modular-invariant ratios and their syzygies, generalizing the insufficient SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$-inspired techniques based solely on polynomials of its absolute invariants. This structure supports a rich landscape of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua. Unlike in the SL$(2,\mathbb Z)$ case, higher-order zeros produce continuous surfaces and curves of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, while, among the six isolated fixed points, only those with $S_4$ and $D_{12}$ residual symmetries can stabilize all three moduli. We also construct isolated vacua away from fixed points, some of which lie at the moduli values preferred by genus-two modular flavor fits, and examine the suppression of the geometric moduli masses near an enhanced-symmetry point.

papers.title: Scalar/axion Wormholes and Boundary Conditions in Gravitational Path Integrals
papers.abstract: Recent work noted that whether or not a given class of spacetime wormholes contributes to the gravitational path integral can depend strongly on the choice of boundary conditions. In particular, for asymptotically-AdS scalar/axion wormholes with spherical boundaries it was suggested that there are regimes where the same wormhole contributes to a Euclidean low-energy effective field theory computation of the partition function $Z_N$ defined by imposing Neumann boundary conditions on the scalar/axion field, while it fails to contribute to a corresponding partition function $Z_D$ defined by imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions on this field. Here we investigate toy models of related wormholes associated with JT gravity coupled to a scalar field, asymptotically-AdS gravity coupled to an axion/scalar with toroidal boundary conditions, and asymptotically flat gravity coupled to an axion/scalar. In all cases we compare $Z_D$ and $Z_N$ as computed in a truncated low-energy effective theory by an appropriate integral over constrained wormholes. In each case we find that, even though $Z_D$ and $Z_N$ are related by an integral transform, the two generally receive contributions from differing sets of saddles. Along the way, we uncover a variety of additional interesting subtleties associated with semiclassical contributions to our $Z_D$ and $Z_N$.

papers.title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
papers.abstract: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal method. This same method also enables one to recover a well defined perturbation theory in quantum gravity, and particularly for asymptotically AdS spacetimes \cite{Witten:2022xxp}. Thus we construct the perturbation theory on these backgrounds in addition to exploring ER=EPR when $G_{N}=0$, in the limit it is perturbatively small and beyond perturbation theory.

papers.title: Folded out-of-time-order correlators in double-scaled SYK
papers.abstract: Harlow and Zhao arXiv:2607.14215 have identified ``anti-scrambling'' as a characteristic signature of cosmological horizons in de Sitter space, and proposed that it can be realized in a quantum system with bounded energy by Euclidean time ``folding" of out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs). We implement this prescription in the DSSYK model. We use arXiv:2303.03474 to define an infinite-temperature ($\beta=0$) DSSYK OTOC that in the semiclassical limit of small values of the double-scaling parameter $\lambda$ reproduces the usual AdS eikonal shockwave behavior with its characteristic time delay, and then apply the Harlow-Zhao fold with the ``fake'' DSSYK inverse temperature $\beta_f$ playing the role of $\beta$. We demonstrate both numerically and analytically that the resulting folded OTOC displays anti-scrambling. The exact DSSYK evaluation tracks the semiclassical de Sitter eikonal formula in the scrambling regime, including a time advance instead of a time delay.The direction of the fold selects the side from which the continued eikonal amplitude approaches its branch cut. We show how our results are consistent with recent ``no-go" constraints. We compare the folded correlator with the two-shell analysis of arXiv:2607.14215: the growing term of the two-shell dilaton invariant appears in DSSYK with the same exponent, but as an imaginary part, while its real part, which would signal the backreaction that ends in a crunch, only moves by $O(\lambda)$ for thermal-scale probes. We also generalize to finite $\beta$; we find reasonable agreement with the de Sitter eikonal form for sufficiently high temperatures, but at lower temperatures the folded correlator is dominated by a pair of complex conjugate saddles, an anti-Stokes crossover that prevents retrieval of the eikonal behavior from the folded OTOC.

papers.title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory.
